title: Wallets, rewards, and payout evidence
outcome: Follow the evidence from a block reward or pool balance to a confirmed transaction.
show: Draw separate boxes for work, payout record, on-chain transaction, and receiving wallet.
concepts: The Bitcoin coinbase transaction can claim the block subsidy and transaction fees under network rules. A pool can distribute proceeds according to its own published payment terms.
A public address can help check receipt on-chain. Wallet keys authorize spending. Keep seed phrases and private keys outside the exercise.
A pool dashboard shows accounting. A transaction ID can locate a broadcast transaction. Confirmation shows inclusion in the chain, and wallet control requires separate evidence.
replicate: Given a sample share counter, pool balance, and transaction ID, label which item answers each question about work, accounting, and payment.
Write which piece of evidence is still missing if the sample has no transaction ID or only an unconfirmed transaction.
check: Which item can you use to look up a payment on a block explorer?
A transaction ID. Check its network, outputs, and confirmation status together.
